lessons.title: The recon mindset
lessons.body: Before attacking anything you map it: which hosts are alive, which ports are open, what software and versions answer. Every open port is a service; every service is a version; every version may have known bugs. Recon is just disciplined curiosity, and it is the same whether you are attacking a lab or defending your own network.

tools.name: nmap
tools.what: The standard port scanner and service mapper. Finds live hosts, open ports, service versions, and OS guesses. Open = a program answers (SYN-ACK); closed = RST; filtered = no reply (firewall). A SYN scan (-sS) is fast and never completes the handshake.
tools.legal: Only run this against machines you own or have explicit written permission to test. Scanning or attacking other systems is illegal.
tools.install: Preinstalled on Kali; else `sudo apt install nmap` / `brew install nmap`.
tools.exercise: Scan your own machine with -sV. For each open port, name the program and decide whether it should be open. That question is network hardening in one line.

tools.name: masscan
tools.what: An internet-scale asynchronous scanner - like nmap but built for huge address ranges at high packet rates. Use it to find live ports fast, then hand those to nmap -sV for detail.
tools.legal: Only run this against machines you own or have explicit written permission to test. Scanning or attacking other systems is illegal.
tools.exercise: On your lab subnet, masscan for open 80/443, then re-scan just those hosts with nmap -sV. Notice the speed-vs-detail tradeoff.
